name: ElevenLabs
summary: Speech synthesis platform known for voices that survive long paragraphs, plus cloning, dubbing and agents.
description:
ElevenLabs built its reputation on the part of text-to-speech that used to be unlistenable: prosody across long passages, breath and pause placement, and a clone that keeps an individual's timbre instead of producing a cousin of it. That is why it ended up behind audiobook pipelines, character voices in games, and a lot of product narration.

The commercial layer matters as much as the audio here. Cloning requires consent in their terms, and the practical risk of a voice tool is reputational rather than technical, so read the licence section for the plan you buy rather than the marketing page. Pricing is character-based and the tiers differ mostly in sample rate, concurrency and cloning rights, which is a confusing way to price things until you are the one estimating a monthly bill.
